mutant.description: Two mutants run against scratch copies of DEPRECATION.md (never against the committed file). For AC1: every case-insensitive 'terminus' replaced with 'ENDPOINT' and AC1's exact invocation re-run. For AC2: a first attempt truncated the file to 5 lines, which did NOT drop AC2 to zero (the title line itself contains 'TERMINUS' but not 'age'; a second, correct mutant replaced every case-insensitive 'age' with 'ZZZ' and AC2's exact invocation was re-run against that copy.
mutant.expected: The terminus-stripped copy must drop AC1's count to 0, below the required 1. The age-stripped copy must drop AC2's count to 0, below the required 1.
mutant.observed: Terminus-stripped copy: AC1 invocation returned 0 (rc=1) -- would FAIL AC1's >=1 bound. Age-stripped copy: AC2 invocation returned 0 (rc=1) -- would FAIL AC2's >=1 bound. Both mutants fired as designed. (The 5-line-truncation mutant tried first for AC1 returned 2, not 0 -- recorded because it is itself informative: the document's own title carries the word, so a naive truncation mutant is a weaker control than a targeted term-substitution one; the term-substitution mutant is the one that actually discriminates and is reported as the control.)
